original_question: Let Γq be the groupoid of the germs of local diffeomorphisms of Rq , and Gq ⊂ Γq be the subgroup fixing 0. Let B Ḡq be the homotopy-theoretic fibre of the map BGq → BGLq (R) classifying the normal bundle of the universal Gq -structure. Is B Ḡq homotopically trivial in B Γ̄q ?
target_in_paper: Section 9.1, Question 9.3 (“Foliations with only one leaf”: Tsuboi [Tsu84b]).
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core target well: it is about the smooth Haefliger-classifying-space problem attached to germs of local diffeomorphisms of R^q, singles out the subgroup fixing 0, and asks whether the corresponding classifying space is homotopically trivial in the ambient foliation-classifying space. That is the right neighborhood in the paper, and it is indeed the problem immediately identified there as the more general older question underlying the nearby Hurder–Vogt question.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is in the smooth C^∞, orientation-preserving setting: it uses Γ_q^+, the groupoid of germs of orientation-preserving local diffeomorphisms of R^q, not an unoriented Γ_q.
The subgroup is denoted Γ_q^0 ⊂ Γ_q^+, the isotropy subgroup fixing 0. Your notation G_q is not the paper’s notation.
The paper asks the question in BΓ_q^+, not in B\bar{Γ}_q. Earlier context defines B\bar{Γ}_q as the fiber of BΓ_q → BO(q), but Question 9.3 itself is not stated in that fiber notation.

Likewise, the paper does not formulate Question 9.3 using the homotopy-theoretic fiber B\bar{G}_q of BG_q → BGL_q(R). Introducing B\bar{G}_q builds in an identification that is not the official nearby statement.
To make the question stand alone, one should say that “homotopically trivial in BΓ_q^+” means that the inclusion-induced classifying map BΓ_q^0 → BΓ_q^+ is null-homotopic.
The orientability condition is hidden in your draft but explicit in the paper: the equivalent geometric formulation concerns orientable Haefliger structures.

The nearby context defines a codimension-q Haefliger structure as a rank-q real vector bundle E → M together with a germ, along the zero section, of a codimension-q foliation transverse to the fibers; this is the ambient meaning of the question.

The question is posed as a family in q; the paper notes only that Tsuboi solved the case q = 1 positively, so if one wants the open part only, that would be q ≥ 2, but the official statement itself is for general q.
refined_question: For each integer q ≥ 1, let Γ_q^+ be the groupoid of germs of orientation-preserving local C^∞ diffeomorphisms of R^q, and let Γ_q^0 ⊂ Γ_q^+ be the isotropy subgroup fixing 0. Is the inclusion-induced classifying map BΓ_q^0 → BΓ_q^+ null-homotopic; equivalently, is BΓ_q^0 homotopically trivial inside BΓ_q^+?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: is every orientable codimension-q Haefliger structure whose microfoliation has the zero section as a leaf homotopically trivial?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Question 9.3, not Question 9.2 or the broader Haefliger–Thurston conjecture. The decisive cue is the subgroup of germs fixing 0; this is exactly the object in Question 9.3, where the paper asks whether BΓ_q^0 is homotopically trivial in BΓ_q^+. The nearby context in Section 9.1 supplies the meaning of Haefliger structures, microfoliations, and the role of BΓ_q and B\bar{Γ}_q. The paper also explicitly says that Question 9.2 is a special case of this more general older question, confirming that Question 9.3 is the nearest official target. Your draft is close in mathematical spirit, but to stay paper-faithful it should use the paper’s orientation-preserving notation and ambient classifying space BΓ_q^+, rather than the fiber-model notation B\bar{G}_q and B\bar{Γ}_q.
